description: Turn a person's own words about themselves into the structured facts the eligibility tools accept. Pass their sentence verbatim ("I'm a nurse at a Tulsa hospital, I live in Broken Arrow, my late father was a TTCU member") and this returns each fact it could read, with the exact words it read it from, a confidence, and a needs_confirmation flag. THIS DOES NOT DECIDE ELIGIBILITY and never returns a credit union: it only fills in fields. Show the extracted facts to the user and get confirmation on every fact with needs_confirmation=true (family relationships, relatives' employers and associations, applicant kind, and asserted qualifiers are always flagged, because a wrong reading of those changes the answer). Then pass `person_search_body` — plus whatever the user confirmed — to find_eligible_credit_unions, which is what actually decides. If extraction is unavailable you get facts: [] and no eligibility signal at all; ask the user for fields directly instead. `confidence` is the extraction model's own uncalibrated self-report and gates only autofill — quote `evidence.quote` to the user, not the number. This call costs 3 API units.

known_facts.description: Optional. Fields you already know, in PersonSearch shape. These are echoed as source="supplied" and never overwritten.

text.description: The person's own words, up to 2000 characters. Do not paraphrase or pre-structure it — the extractor needs the original sentence to anchor evidence spans.

name: extract_eligibility_facts

billed_units.description: API units billed for this call: 3 for a live extraction, 0 for a sandbox fixture.

confidence_is_model_self_reported.description: Always true when present. A standing warning that 'confidence' is the model's own number, not a measured accuracy.

confirmation_required.description: True when anything needs confirming. Show the facts to the user before searching.

extraction_available.description: False when extraction was unavailable. That carries no eligibility signal whatsoever - ask the user for fields directly, never read it as a negative answer.

extractor_version.description: Version of the extractor's prompt and post-processing.

facts.description: Facts read from the person's words, each returned FOR CONFIRMATION. Never a decision, and never a credit union.

confidence.description: The extraction model's own uncalibrated self-report, 0-1. It gates autofill only. Quote the evidence to the user, not this number.

conflict_with.description: Set when this value contradicts one you supplied in known_facts. Both are returned; no winner is picked.

evidence.description: The words in the user's own text this fact was read from.

end.description: Character offset one past the quote's last character.

start.description: Character offset of the quote's first character in the text you sent.

field.description: A field name that find_eligible_credit_unions accepts, e.g. 'occupation' or 'home_state'.

needs_confirmation.description: True when the user must confirm this before it is relied on. Always true for family relationships, relatives' details, applicant kind and asserted qualifiers.

note.description: A plain-language question or explanation to put to the user.

source.description: 'extracted' (read from the text) or 'supplied' (echoed from known_facts, untouched).

value.description: The typed value, coerced deterministically from what the person said. null means it could not be turned into a usable value - ask the user, do not guess.

note.description: Standing disclosure plus the next step: confirm the flagged facts, then call find_eligible_credit_unions.

person_search_body.description: A ready-to-send argument set for find_eligible_credit_unions, containing only confirmed-or-supplied facts. Add the user's confirmations to it before calling.

sandbox.description: True when this is the frozen sandbox fixture rather than a real extraction.

unparsed_spans.description: Phrases recognized as meaningful but not mapped to a field, including anything said in the past tense or hypothetically. Ask about these.

end.description: Character offset one past the last character.

note.description: Why it was not turned into a fact, and what to ask.

quote.description: The phrase, verbatim from the text.

start.description: Character offset of the first character.
